gaps.sentence: We had no ___ signed the lease than the landlord sold the building.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner … than' — here with 'had' before the participle.

gaps.sentence: Under no circumstances ___ the door be left unlocked.
gaps.explanation: 'Under no circumstances should/must the door be left unlocked' — modal + inversion.

gaps.sentence: So convinced ___ he of his innocence that he refused the deal.
gaps.explanation: 'So convinced was he of …' — inversion after fronted 'so + adj'.

gaps.sentence: ___ I richer, I would travel the world.
gaps.explanation: Were I richer = If I were richer — formal inversion.

gaps.sentence: Little did the suspects ___ that the police were listening.
gaps.explanation: 'Little did they know' — 'know' as bare verb after the inverted auxiliary 'did'.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the play cancelled, but the theatre was closed as well.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only was the play cancelled' — inverted passive.

gaps.sentence: ___ you require assistance, please do not hesitate to contact the desk.
gaps.explanation: 'Should you require …' = 'If you should require …' — formal inverted conditional.

gaps.sentence: Little ___ anyone realise how close the firm was to insolvency.
gaps.explanation: "Little did anyone realise" = nobody realised — emphatic inversion with do-support.
